title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for history of pulmonary embolism.

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is a 78-year-old male who presented three years ago with a pulmonary embolism. He was started on a course of medications which was completed. He reports no shortness of breath or chest pain since the initial episode. He states the condition has resolved.

Update: The patient reports he feels well today and denies any new respiratory symptoms. He is here for a routine check-up.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Respiratory: Negative
Cardiovascular: Negative
Gastrointestinal: Negative
Musculoskeletal: Negative
Neurological: Negative

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented.
Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes or crackles.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs.

Assessment:
1. History of pulmonary embolism, resolved.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications.
2. Return to clinic in 6 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: A pulmonary embolism that resolved after completed treatment: personal history, Z86.711 (no HCC).

distractors.why: There is no current embolism: code the history.
